n: Jerusalem is under siege and humiliated: enemies strike Israel’s ruler on the cheek with a rod. Christians also see a foreshadowing of how the true Judge of Israel, Jesus, would be struck.

f.g: Jerusalem, pictured as a city of soldiers — or one now gashing itself in grief.

f.w: smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek

n: One of the Bible’s clearest messianic prophecies: from little Bethlehem will come Israel’s Ruler, whose origins are “from everlasting.” The chief priests cited this verse to Herod, and it was fulfilled in Jesus’s birth.

f.g: Bethlehem in the district of Ephrathah, David’s hometown, about 6 miles south of Jerusalem.

f.w: out of thee shall he come forth

n: Israel will be given up to enemies until “she who is in labor” gives birth — then the scattered brothers will return. The birth points to the coming Messiah.

f.w: she which travaileth hath brought forth

n: This Ruler will shepherd His flock in the Lord’s strength and majesty. His people will live securely, for His greatness will reach the ends of the earth.

f.w: great unto the ends of the earth

n: “He shall be our peace.” When invaders come, God will raise up more than enough leaders to repel them. “Seven… eight” is a Hebrew way of saying “plenty.”

f.w: this man shall be the peace
seven shepherds, and eight principal men
f.g: A numerical pattern meaning “more than enough.”

n: These leaders will defeat Assyria, “the land of Nimrod.” The Assyrian here stands for every great enemy of God’s people.
The scattered remnant of Jacob will be a blessing among many nations, like dew and gentle rain from the Lord — refreshing, and coming by God’s timing, not man’s.

f.w: as a dew from the LORD

n: But the same remnant will also be like a lion among sheep. The resurrected Savior quoted this verse twice to the Nephites, applying it to the latter days and the remnant of Jacob in the Americas.

f.w: as a lion among the beasts of the forest

n: God’s people will triumph over their enemies.

f.w: Thine hand shall be lifted up

n: Then God will remove the things His people trusted instead of Him — first horses and chariots, their military might. The Savior quoted verses 10–14 in 3 Nephi 21.

f.w: I will cut off thy horses

n: He will remove fortified cities and strongholds — false securities.

f.w: throw down all thy strong holds

n: He will get rid of sorcery and fortune-tellers, which tried to get guidance apart from God.
Carved idols and sacred pillars will be destroyed. People will stop worshiping things they made with their own hands.

f.g: Sacred stone pillars used in pagan worship.

n: He will uproot the Asherah poles — wooden symbols of a fertility goddess — and destroy the cities devoted to idolatry.

f.g: Hebrew asherim — wooden poles honoring the goddess Asherah.

n: Finally, God will bring justice on the nations that refuse to obey. The Savior added “who have not heard” in 3 Nephi 21:21, connecting it to those who reject His latter-day work.
